segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so quick gut check on the Havenridge renewal. They want to add 18 seats, move from 72 to 90 total, and keep the same May 1 go-live for the analytics module.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Is the pricing sheet lining up with what we quoted last week?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Mostly. The subscription comes to $54,600 annually after the 8% expansion discount. Services is $6,200 for onboarding, billed once. The buyer is fine with that, but the deal is just sitting because I still don't have the payment terms exception approved.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah. And I've nudged finance twice, deal desk once, and legal this morning because the redline has the same clause. I sent the invoice history, the credit note from February, all of it. The customer asked me again today if we can send signature pages by Friday, and I can't move it out of verbal until someone signs off. It's been stalled since Tuesday over this one answer.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Got it. Who owns the actual yes or no?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Finance owns the terms, legal just wants to know if they can leave the language in. I don't need anything fancy, just approve net-60 for the first year or tell me no so I can go back with net-45.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: I'll message Maria in finance and copy you. If she approves, can you get procurement the final order form same day?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep. Order form is already drafted in the CRM, effective April 30, 12-month term, auto-renew off. I just need to update the payment terms field and attach the services SOW.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay, send me the account notes and the invoice numbers. I'll push on it before their 2 p.m. cutover meeting.
